title: Telemetry Frontdoor: reduce syscall overhead for metrics ingestion and modernize tracing hooks
creator: Leah Patel
description: Reduce per-request syscall and lock overhead from the runtimeobservability hotpath by introducing a lightweight telemetry-frontdoor process and incrementally modernizing tracing hooks to a nonblocking handoff model. The goal is to lower 95th/99th token-cost and CPU tail while preserving signal fidelity for alerts and postmortems.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Palo Alto sync: scoped problem to two hotspots identified from production sampling: (1) metrics/label emission path is doing per-request write() syscalls into journald-like forwarders; (2) tracing hooks executed on hot request path take a mutex to format attributes and sometimes perform small allocations. Both add measurable tail for small-response workloads.

2026-02-20 - Spike results: implemented userspace ringbuf (mmap + memfd) for metric writes in a prototype. End-to-end microbenchmark (p50/p95 token emit) shows ~18% p95 reduction, and CPU syscalls per second reduced by ~40% on a 4-GPU dedicated node. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/re-runtime/pull/4512 (WIP).

2026-02-25 - Design decision: prefer a thin telemetry-frontdoor binary running as a sidecar-style daemon (single-threaded I/O loop) instead of in-process aggregator. Trade-offs: reduces per-request syscalls and locks but introduces a process boundary and a small fixed memory footprint. Chosen because it isolates crashes and allows easier language-agnostic instrumentation in future.

2026-03-02 - Tracing hook plan: change tracing hook from synchronous attribute formatting to a handoff that copies a compact representation into the ringbuf and defers heavy formatting to the frontdoor. This preserves attribute completeness while moving allocations off the hotpath. Will land behind feature-flag `telemetry.frontdoor.enabled`.

2026-03-05 - Security review note: frontdoor reads memfd-backed ring buffers and forwards telemetry to existing OTLP exporter endpoints. Confirmed no secrets are written to the ringbuf. Working with security to add a KMS-backed signer for exported envelopes in a follow-up (assigned to security team).

2026-03-08 - Implementation: added memfd-backed circular buffer with wrap-safe header, fixed-size slots for common metric types, and a small freelist for dynamic attributes. Initial allocator avoids malloc for common codepaths. See code branch: feature/telemetry-frontdoor and draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/re-runtime/pull/4589

2026-03-10 - Perf benchmark: synthetic workload (100 RPS, short completions) shows p95 latency improvment from 28ms -> 23ms and per-token CPU usage down ~12%. Integration test run on staging matched synthetic results. Found regression: rare full-buffer stalls when batch flush coincides with huge-burst workloads; mitigated by backpressure metric and a best-effort drop policy for non-critical counters.

2026-03-12 - Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated pool smallset (10 nodes) with telemetry.frontdoor.enabled=true and frontdoor loglevel=info. Monitor metrics: telemetry.buffer.drop_rate, telemetry.frontdoor.flush_latency, runtime.request_p95. If drop_rate exceeds 0.5% or request_p95 regresses >5% revert.

2026-03-13 - Code review feedback: PM requested an E2E dashboard for comparing raw vs frontdoor-processed spans to validate signal parity. Design doc added: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Telemetry+Frontdoor+Design. Also requested clearer metrics tagging for rollouts and per-tenant buffer metrics (to detect noisy tenants).

2026-03-14 - Next steps: (1) Address PR comments around edge-case attribute truncation and add unit tests for memfd wrap sequences; (2) implement lightweight per-tenant credits to prevent a single tenant from saturating ringbuf; (3) run 48h soak on canary pool and validate no increase in pager alerts. Owner: Marco. ETA for canary completion: 2026-03-31.
